description: Attach ONE file to a ticket so the support team can see it — typically a diagnostic/log file or a screenshot that documents a bug. Provide the bytes base64-encoded in file_b64 (no data: URI prefix), up to ~3 MB, with content_type one of image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain or application/json. The file is forwarded to a human on the support side; it is not stored or served back, so the result records only the filename and type. Attaching counts as a reply: an answered ticket returns to awaiting a reply, and an auto-closed ticket within 7 days reopens. If the response is attachment_unavailable, retry shortly or continue with reply_support_ticket.

caption.description: Optional note shown with the file (max 400 chars).

content_type.description: File MIME type: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain or application/json.

file_b64.description: The file bytes, base64-encoded (no data: URI prefix). Max ~3 MB decoded.

filename.description: Filename shown to the support team, e.g. 'error.log' or 'screenshot.png'.

name: attach_support_ticket_file

attachment.description: Attached file metadata when the message carries a file, otherwise null.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the last user/admin message (UTC).

opener_type.description: Who opened the ticket, snapshotted from the account type at creation.

status.description: awaiting_reply | answered | closed. `closed` is terminal (an auto-closed ticket can be reopened by replying within 7 days).

title: Attach a file to a support ticket
